capabilities: assign hotkeys to editor API commands
move the cursor by line, character, or to note start/end
indent, unindent, swap, and delete lines
fold and unfold items at the cursor or everywhere
disambiguation: Despite the name, it does not remap existing hotkeys; it adds editor API commands that can then be assigned hotkeys.
extras: Commands only work while an editor is open, the plugin sets no default hotkeys, and Alt is recommended as the modifier for cursor movement since Ctrl/Shift would trigger text selection.
motivation: The author wanted to replicate the Tabout VSCode extension's behavior and, while studying the Obsidian API, decided exposing editor commands as hotkey-assignable commands was a good way to do it.
problem: Many editor API commands have no command palette entry, so they cannot be assigned hotkeys through Obsidian's hotkeys settings.

relations.evidence: The original idea was to replicate the behaviour of the Tabout extension for VSCode

summary: Hotkey mapper that exposes Obsidian editor API commands (cursor moves, indenting, line swaps, folding) for hotkey assignment.
